text: Could you hold one price for 70 years? Coca-Cola did. A Coke cost $0.05 through two world wars.
Why couldn't it rise? In 1899, two lawyers got Coke's bottling rights with the syrup price fixed
permanently. Not exactly a great contract. So why not just charge more? Coke tied its brand to
$0.05 and its vending machines took a single nickel. The next coin up was a dime. Double the
price. And that's not even the strangest part. Coke asked the U.S. Treasury for a
seven and a half cent coin. Its boss even asked his hunting buddy, President
Eisenhower. The answer was no. Inflation finally won. By 1959 the nickel
Coke was gone. The price never moved. Your nickel just kept getting weaker.
